title: Most recent continuation of the same two-symbol context
summary: A table remembers, for every ordered pair of adjacent symbols seen so far, the symbol that followed that pair the last time it occurred. When the current two-symbol context is in the table, the prediction mixes a fixed background distribution with a point mass on the remembered successor; otherwise the background alone is used.
core_idea: Remember the last successor of every two-symbol context and predict it again, mixed with a fixed background distribution.

state.name: R
state.type: table from symbol pairs to symbols
state.meaning: R[(u, v)] is the symbol that followed the adjacent pair (u, v) at its most recent occurrence, or empty.

state.name: q
state.meaning: Fixed background distribution over the V symbols, estimated from training text.

update.name: overwrite
update.plain: R[(x_(t-2), x_(t-1))] = x_t, overwriting any earlier entry for that pair

readout.name: mixture
readout.plain: if the pair (x_(t-1), x_t) is in the table R: p(w) = (1 - lam) q(w) + lam * [w == R[(x_(t-1), x_t)]]; otherwise p(w) = q(w)

learning.description: The background q is the relative frequency of each symbol in the training text (counting), and lam is chosen by grid search on held-out text. Within a sequence only the table changes.
learning.few_shot_argument: One occurrence of a two-symbol context and its successor is enough for the successor to receive probability at least lam the next time the context occurs.

complexity.constants_notes: One table write and one table read per symbol, plus writing the V-entry distribution; the table has at most V^2 entries.

prediction.statement: After one occurrence of (u, v, w), p(w | u, v) >= lam = 0.8 at the next occurrence of (u, v).

capabilities.prediction: Each continuation of a repeated phrase whose two-symbol contexts are distinct is predicted with probability at least lam.

capabilities.task: associative recall of K pairs written as 'a b c' triples
capabilities.prediction: Exact when each probe pair occurs once before the probe, for any K up to V^2 distinct pairs.

known_relatives.name: not assessed
known_relatives.relation: This card does not compare its mechanism with others.
known_relatives.claimed_difference: No difference from earlier work is claimed.

falsifiers: After one occurrence of (u, v, w), the next occurrence of (u, v) gives p(w) below lam.
A context seen twice with different successors predicts the older successor.

toy_example.description: Filling the table on a short sequence and reading the mixture for the last context.
toy_example.python:
import json
V = 4
q = [0.4, 0.3, 0.2, 0.1]
lam = 0.8
seq = [0, 1, 2, 3, 0, 1, 3, 2, 0, 1]
R = {}
for t in range(2, len(seq)):
    R[(seq[t - 2], seq[t - 1])] = seq[t]
ctx = (seq[-2], seq[-1])
p = [(1 - lam) * q[w] + (lam if R.get(ctx) == w else 0.0) for w in range(V)]
print(json.dumps({"successor": R.get(ctx), "p": [round(v, 6) for v in p], "entries": len(R)}))
